subject: Maths
title: SOH CAH TOA — finding angles
subtitle: Trigonometry · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can use inverse trigonometric functions to find unknown angles in right-angled triangles.

key_vocab.definition: To find an unknown angle, use the inverse trig functions: sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹, or tan⁻¹. Choose which ratio to use based on which two sides are known.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can use inverse trigonometric functions to find unknown angles in right-angled triangles.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: unknown angle -- To find an unknown angle, use the inverse trig functions: sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹, or tan⁻¹. Choose which ratio to use based on which two sides are known.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Identify the two known sides, choose the correct ratio, then apply the inverse function.
θ = sin⁻¹(opp ÷ hyp)
Or cos⁻¹(adj/hyp) or tan⁻¹(opp/adj)

Key examples:
  ✓ opp = 3, hyp = 6: angle = sin⁻¹(3/6) = 30°  (use SOH)
  ✓ adj = 4, hyp = 8: angle = cos⁻¹(4/8) = 60°  (use CAH)
  ✓ opp = 5, adj = 5: angle = tan⁻¹(1) = 45°  (use TOA)
  ✗ Use sin when you have adjacent and hypotenuse  (that is cos (CAH))
  ✗ sin⁻¹(0.5) = 60°  (sin⁻¹(0.5) = 30°)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – using sin inverse
  Find angle x: opposite = 4, hypotenuse = 8.
  Have opposite and hypotenuse: use sin
  sin x = 4/8 = 0.5
  x = sin⁻¹(0.5) = 30°
  x = 30°
  (Opposite and hypotenuse means SOH.)

Example 2 – using cos inverse
  Find angle x: adjacent = 5, hypotenuse = 10.
  Have adjacent and hypotenuse: use cos
  cos x = 5/10 = 0.5
  x = cos⁻¹(0.5) = 60°
  x = 60°
  (Adjacent and hypotenuse means CAH.)

sections.content:

sections.content:
Find angle x in each triangle (1 dp where needed).

(b) opp = 5, hyp = 13
(c) adj = 8, hyp = 10
(d) opp = 12, adj = 9
(e) opp = 1, hyp = 2

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ To find an angle, use the inverse trig function
✗ sin⁻¹(0.5) = 60°
✓ tan⁻¹(1) = 45°
✗ Use SOH when you know the adjacent and hypotenuse
✓ cos⁻¹(0.5) = 60°
